voiceSample: My daughter is exhausted all the time, even after a full night's sleep.
openingMessage: Why is {name} so exhausted all the time?
readyLine: Thank you — that gives me a clear picture of {name}'s days. My assessment is ready.
suggestedQuestions: Could low iron explain the tiredness?
How much sleep does a teenager really need?
What should we ask at the next appointment?

sections.title: What I'm Hearing
sections.body: {name} has been tired for a while, and it isn't lifting with rest. From what was shared, sleep, mood, the cycle and everyday eating may all be playing a part — and together they can add up to a body that never quite recharges.

sections.title: What This May Mean
sections.body: Ongoing tiredness in young people often comes from a mix of things: sleep that isn't restorative, stress or low mood, energy dips from skipped meals, and sometimes low iron or B12 — especially with heavy periods or a vegetarian diet. None of these is a diagnosis; they're worth exploring with {name}'s provider.

sections.title: Questions for {name}'s Provider
bullets: Could we check iron, ferritin and B12?
Could any of the medicines or supplements affect sleep or energy?
Is the cycle part of the picture, and is the bleeding normal for her age?
What would help with sleep and stress right now?

sections.title: Small Things to Try This Week
bullets: A regular wind-down time, with screens off an hour before bed.
A simple breakfast, even something small.
A short check-in each evening about how the day felt.

sections.title: A Word From Deborah
sections.body: Paying attention to this is the right instinct. Small, steady changes — and the right questions at the next appointment — usually make a real difference.

followUps.reply: Low iron and B12 are common causes of tiredness, especially with heavy periods or a vegetarian diet. A simple blood test with {name}'s provider can check both.
Most teenagers need around eight to ten hours. Late screens and stress are the usual things that cut into it.

fallbackReply: That's a good question to bring to {name}'s provider. I can help put it into words for the appointment.
